In order to prevent the cylinders from rolling, two wooden stakes are fixed on both sides of the cylinders. Neglecting all friction, it can be known from this that (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The force exerted by the wooden stake on the cylinder is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}mg$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, three completely identical cylinders are placed. Each cylinder has mass m and cross-sectional radius R. In order to prevent the cylinders from rolling, two wooden stakes are fixed on both sides of the cylinders. Neglect all friction; what is the magnitude of the force exerted by the wooden stake on the cylinder?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The force exerted by the wooden stake on the cylinder is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}mg$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three completely identical cylinder cross-sectional circles, two placed side by side below on the horizontal ground, and one above, wedged between the two lower cylinders; on the left and right sides there is respectively one vertical wooden stake blocking the lower cylinders, and the whole is left-right symmetric. The cylinders are in mutual contact, and friction is neglected, so the contact forces are all along the direction of the line connecting the centers of the two circles. Reasoning: The three cylinders have the same radius and are in mutual contact, so the three centers form an equilateral triangle with side length 2R, and the line connecting the center of the upper cylinder and either lower cylinder makes 60° with the horizontal. First analyze the upper cylinder, and let the supporting force of each lower cylinder on the upper cylinder be N. By left-right symmetry, the two N have equal magnitude; the horizontal components cancel each other, and vertical equilibrium is: 2N sin60° = mg. Therefore N = mg/(2 sin60°) = mg/√3. Then analyze the lower-left cylinder: the pressure exerted on it by the upper cylinder also has magnitude N, and its direction is obliquely left downward along the line connecting the centers, with horizontal component magnitude N cos60°. The supporting force of the ground on the lower cylinder is vertically upward and cannot balance the horizontal direction; when there is no friction, the left wooden stake only provides a horizontal force F to balance this horizontal component. Therefore F = N cos60° = (mg/√3)·(1/2) = √3 mg/6. The right wooden stake is the same.
